initial_requirements: The Gaia science-processing community needs a fast simulator that can generate catalog, auxiliary, intermediate, and statistically representative final-mission data for Gaia instruments. Users should be able to select the processing stage and relevant error models, produce large simulated datasets without running the full telemetry and mission-database chain, and deliver results compatible with the wider Gaia processing environment as scientific models evolve.

turns.interviewer_utterance: What are the primary goals and success criteria for this Gaia simulator, and which outcomes matter most—for example speed, fidelity, scalability, compatibility with Gaia processing tools, or support for evolving scientific models?
turns.interviewee_utterance:
The main goal is to give the Gaia science-processing community a fast way to generate realistic data products at different processing stages without having to run the full telemetry and mission-database chain. Success really means people can produce large simulated datasets quickly, with the right level of realism for the stage they’re studying, and have those outputs plug into the wider Gaia processing environment without friction.
If I had to rank the outcomes, speed and scalability are very important because the simulator has to handle large volumes efficiently, but fidelity also matters because the data need to be scientifically representative. Compatibility with Gaia processing tools is essential, and it also has to stay adaptable as the scientific models evolve, otherwise it becomes obsolete too quickly.

turns.interviewer_utterance: Which processing stages should users be able to choose from in the simulator, and how should they configure the relevant error models for each stage—for example, should the selection be fixed to a known set of stages, and what level of control should users have over parameters, presets, or defaults?
turns.interviewee_utterance:
We definitely need a defined set of processing stages rather than an open-ended free-for-all, because the simulator has to stay aligned with the Gaia pipeline. The obvious ones are catalog, auxiliary, intermediate, and a statistically representative final-mission output, but I’d expect the exact list to be whatever the project team agrees is supported.
For error models, users should be able to pick the model appropriate to the chosen stage and then adjust the main parameters where that makes scientific sense. I’d lean toward providing sensible defaults and presets for common use cases, with advanced control exposed only for users who need it, because not everyone will want to tune every parameter by hand.

slots.name: project_goals
slots.value: Provide the Gaia science-processing community with a fast way to generate realistic data products at different processing stages without running the full telemetry and mission-database chain; enable users to produce large simulated datasets quickly with the right level of realism for the stage being studied, while ensuring outputs integrate smoothly with the wider Gaia processing environment and remain adaptable as scientific models evolve.

slots.name: stakeholder_roles
slots.value: Gaia science-processing community; project team responsible for defining the supported processing stages; users who configure stage-specific error models, with advanced users needing deeper parameter control.

slots.name: functional_needs
slots.value: Support generation of simulated data products at defined processing stages; allow users to select from a project-approved set of stages; let users choose stage-appropriate error models and adjust key parameters; provide sensible defaults and presets for common use cases with advanced controls for expert users; produce large simulated datasets efficiently; integrate with the wider Gaia processing environment; remain adaptable to evolving scientific models.

slots.name: business_rules
slots.value: Processing stages must come from a defined, project-approved set aligned with the Gaia pipeline; error models must match the selected stage; defaults and presets should be provided for common use cases, with advanced parameter control only where scientifically justified.

slots.name: data_entities
slots.value: Simulated Gaia data products at multiple processing stages, including catalog, auxiliary, intermediate, and statistically representative final-mission data.

slots.name: constraints
slots.value: Must not require running the full telemetry and mission-database chain; must use a defined set of processing stages aligned with the Gaia pipeline; must be fast and scalable; outputs must be compatible with Gaia processing tools/environment; must support evolving scientific models.

slots.name: quality_concerns
slots.value: Speed, scalability, scientific fidelity/realism, compatibility with Gaia processing tools, and adaptability to evolving models.

slots.name: boundary_conditions
slots.value: Users should not be able to choose arbitrary or open-ended processing stages; supported stages are limited to the project-approved set.

slots.name: performance_targets
slots.value: The simulator should generate large simulated datasets quickly and handle large volumes efficiently.

slots.name: output_formats_and_interfaces
slots.value: Outputs must plug into and be compatible with the wider Gaia processing environment and Gaia processing tools without friction.

slots.name: processing_stage_selection
slots.value: Users can select from a defined, project-approved set of processing stages aligned with the Gaia pipeline, including catalog, auxiliary, intermediate, and statistically representative final-mission output.

slots.name: error_model_configuration
slots.value: Users can choose the error model appropriate to the selected processing stage, adjust the main scientifically relevant parameters, and rely on sensible defaults and presets for common use cases; advanced tuning is available for expert users.

slots.name: scientific_model_update_governance
slots.value: The simulator must stay adaptable as scientific models evolve so it does not become obsolete too quickly.
